regimens.indication: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Hypothyroidism — Adults (including Geriatric and Cardiac Disease)

refs.quote: SYNTHROID is indicated in adult and pediatric patients, including neonates, as a replacement therapy in primary (thyroidal), secondary (pituitary), and tertiary (hypothalamic) congenital or acquired hypothyroidism.

Adults diagnosed with hypothyroidism Full replacement dose is 1.6 mcg/kg/day. Some patients require a lower starting dose. Titrate dosage by 12.5 to 25 mcg increments every 4 to 6 weeks, as needed until the patient is euthyroid.

dose.frequency: once daily on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast

regimens.dose_text: Full replacement dose: 1.6 mcg/kg/day orally once daily on an empty stomach, 30–60 minutes before breakfast (at least 4 hours apart from drugs interfering with absorption). Titrate by 12.5 to 25 mcg increments every 4 to 6 weeks until euthyroid (dosages >200 mcg/day seldom required). In geriatric patients or adults with underlying cardiac disease or risk of atrial fibrillation, start at <1.6 mcg/kg/day and titrate every 6 to 8 weeks.

regimens.indication: Pituitary TSH Suppression in Well-Differentiated Thyroid Cancer — Adults and Pediatrics

refs.quote: SYNTHROID is indicated in adult and pediatric patients, including neonates, as an adjunct to surgery and radioiodine therapy in the management of thyrotropin-dependent well-differentiated thyroid cancer.

TSH Suppression in Well-differentiated Thyroid Cancer in Adult and Pediatric Patients The SYNTHROID dosage is based on the target level of TSH suppression for the stage and clinical status of thyroid cancer.

regimens.dose_text: Dosage is individualized based on the target level of TSH suppression for the stage and clinical status of thyroid cancer, as an adjunct to surgery and radioiodine therapy.

value: NOT FOR TREATMENT OF OBESITY OR FOR WEIGHT LOSS: Thyroid hormones, including SYNTHROID, either alone or with other therapeutic agents, should not be used for the treatment of obesity or for weight loss. In euthyroid patients, doses within daily hormonal requirements are ineffective for weight reduction; larger doses may produce serious or even life-threatening manifestations of toxicity, particularly with sympathomimetic amines.

Oral levothyroxine sodium is a synthetic T4 hormone that exerts the same physiologic effect as endogenous T4, thereby maintaining normal T4 levels when a deficiency is present.

mg_safety.note: Synthetic T4 replacement hormone with no neuromuscular junction blocking activity.

mechanism_of_action.value: Synthetic L-thyroxine (T4) hormone that controls DNA transcription and protein synthesis via nuclear thyroid receptor binding; predominantly converted to triiodothyronine (T3, ~80%) by peripheral deiodination.

refs.quote: Triiodothyronine (T3) and L-thyroxine (T4) diffuse into the cell nucleus and bind to thyroid receptor proteins attached to DNA. This hormone nuclear receptor complex activates gene transcription and synthesis of messenger RNA and cytoplasmic proteins.

value.effect: Bind levothyroxine in the GI tract and decrease absorption, potentially resulting in hypothyroidism.
value.management: Administer SYNTHROID at least 4 hours before or after these agents.

value.management: Monitor patients appropriately for changes in thyroid function.

refs.quote: Sucralfate, antacids and proton pump inhibitors may cause hypochlorhydria, affect intragastric pH, and reduce levothyroxine absorption. Monitor patients appropriately.

value.effect: Phenobarbital (UGT induction) and rifampin accelerate hepatic T4 degradation; phenytoin and carbamazepine displace T4 from serum protein binding, reducing total and free T4 by 20% to 40%.
value.management: Closely monitor thyroid hormone parameters and adjust SYNTHROID dose as needed.

refs.quote: Phenytoin and carbamazepine reduce serum protein binding of levothyroxine, and total and free T4 may be reduced by 20% to 40%, but most patients have normal serum TSH levels and are clinically euthyroid. Closely monitor thyroid hormone parameters.

value.effect: SYNTHROID increases the response to oral anticoagulant therapy.
value.management: A decrease in anticoagulant dose may be warranted when correcting hypothyroidism or increasing SYNTHROID dose; closely monitor coagulation tests.

refs.quote: SYNTHROID increases the response to oral anticoagulant therapy. Therefore, a decrease in the dose of anticoagulant may be warranted with correction of the hypothyroid state or when the SYNTHROID dose is increased. Closely monitor coagulation tests to permit appropriate and timely dosage adjustments.

value.effect: TCAs/tetracyclics + SYNTHROID increase therapeutic and toxic effects of both (cardiac arrhythmias, CNS stimulation); sertraline may increase SYNTHROID requirements.
value.management: Monitor for cardiac arrhythmias/CNS toxicity with TCAs; monitor TSH and adjust SYNTHROID dose with sertraline.

refs.quote: Concurrent use of tricyclic (e.g., amitriptyline) or tetracyclic (e.g., maprotiline) antidepressants and SYNTHROID may increase the therapeutic and toxic effects of both drugs, possibly due to increased receptor sensitivity to catecholamines.

value.effect: Sympathomimetics increase risk of coronary insufficiency in CAD patients; ketamine + SYNTHROID may produce marked hypertension and tachycardia.
value.management: Closely monitor blood pressure, heart rate, and cardiac ischemia risk.

refs.quote: Concurrent use of ketamine and SYNTHROID may produce marked hypertension and tachycardia. Closely monitor blood pressure and heart rate in these patients.

value.effect: SYNTHROID may worsen glycemic control (increasing antidiabetic/insulin requirements) and decrease serum digitalis glycoside levels.
value.management: Monitor glycemic control and digitalis levels/response closely when starting, changing, or discontinuing SYNTHROID.

refs.quote: Addition of SYNTHROID therapy in patients with diabetes mellitus may worsen glycemic control and result in increased antidiabetic agent or insulin requirements. Carefully monitor glycemic control, especially when thyroid therapy is started, changed, or discontinued

value.effect: Amiodarone, high-dose propranolol, and glucocorticoids decrease peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion; TKIs (imatinib) may cause hypothyroidism; biotin interferes with TSH/T4/T3 immunoassays.
value.management: Stop biotin at least 2 days before thyroid testing; monitor TSH/free-T4 with TKIs or amiodarone.

refs.quote: Biotin supplementation is known to interfere with thyroid hormone immunoassays that are based on a biotin and streptavidin interaction, which may result in erroneous thyroid hormone test results. Stop biotin and biotin-containing supplements for at least 2 days prior to thyroid testing.

tier.note: Clinical experience including postmarketing studies in pregnant women treated with oral levothyroxine to maintain euthyroid state has not reported increased rates of major birth defects, miscarriages, or adverse maternal/fetal outcomes. SYNTHROID should not be discontinued during pregnancy, and untreated maternal hypothyroidism adversely affects fetal neurocognitive development.

Published studies report that levothyroxine is present in human milk following the administration of oral levothyroxine. No adverse effects on the breastfed infant have been reported and there is no information on the effects of levothyroxine on milk production. Adequate levothyroxine treatment during lactation may normalize milk production in hypothyroid lactating mothers with low milk supply.
